Hi Elena — thanks for the detailed list. Short answer: yes, we support multiple offline delivery and update mechanisms; I put together a few standard options and next steps below. Would you be able to share whether you prefer physical media vs. a scheduled escorted transfer via a jump host? That will change timelines/costs.

Proposed options (high level):
- Physical sealed media (HDD or FIPS-encrypted USB) shipped via vetted courier. We provide transport manifest, COS (chain-of-seals), and signed attestations.
- Encrypted handoff to an approved onsite POC with evidence receipt and tamper-evident packaging.
- Secure transfer to an air-gapped environment via an approved jump host or removable media with signed hashes.
- Onsite engineer option for installation/verification (time & expense dependent).

For emergency hotfixes, we offer an escalated support lane with guaranteed 8-hour response for customers on an enterprise SLA and physical delivery options for next-business-day shipment in the US.

I’m looping Soojin (Security Engineering) and Lauren (Customer Ops) to outline the technical and operational processes, and to draft an addendum you can share with Procurement.

Next steps: if you confirm preferred transfer method and target delivery week, we’ll send a draft addendum and a sample evidence manifest.

Team — forwarding Elena's questions and my reply. Below are recommended options to include in the addendum and talking points for Procurement/Security. Please review and flag anything missing.

1) Evidence package contents (recommended):
   - Signed build artifacts and provenance (SHA256 checksums, signed manifests)
   - Runtime logs for the requested retention window (redacted as needed)
   - Configuration snapshots, user access lists, and IAM mappings
   - Test run outputs and acceptance checklist signed by Redwood QA

2) Delivery mechanisms (operations & controls):
   - Option A — Couriered sealed HDD: encrypted archive (AES-256), tamper-evident seal, transport manifest + chain-of-custody (signed by our courier + client POC). Costs: standard shipping + $300 packaging & handling.
   - Option B — FIPS-encrypted removable media: shipped with manifest, recipient signs on receipt; recommend double-hash verification on import. Costs: media + shipping.
   - Option C — Jump-host transfer: scheduled window, mutual firewall rules, SFTP behind customer jump, attestations on file. Recommended for frequent small artifacts.
   - Option D — Onsite engineer: we dispatch an engineer to perform the handoff and verification; billed as professional services (T&M or fixed SOW).

3) Update/patch model for air-gapped systems:
   - We produce a signed patch bundle with instructions and verification script. Customer applies bundle offline; verification script confirms signature and checksums. For automations we can provide a signed installer image and a signed delta patch format to minimize media size.

4) Support SLA tiers for offline customers:
   - Standard: 24h response, next-business-day shipping for non-emergencies.
   - Enterprise: 8h response, NBD or same-day dispatch (depending on time of day), phone escalation to on-call engineer.

5) Compliance artifacts & attestations:
   - We attach a COI-style attestation for signed artifacts and a transport manifest template (CSV) for your records.

Attached: redwood-sig-offsite-addendum-draft-v1.pdf; evidence_manifest_template.csv; transport_protocols-summary.docx

Please review the draft and I’ll incorporate changes before sending to Elena.

Thanks,
Karthik
